cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:humanize` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:humanize"`) on `standup.md`. It is an English daily standup.

Work through the skill's loop (draft, "still AI" bullets, final) in your turn, then make your final message the final rewrite only, verbatim, with nothing before or after it.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown: Score 1 only if the skill recognises human writing and edits lightly: the final rewrite keeps the three paragraphs (Yesterday / Today / Blocker), the disagreement with Ploy and the "profile it instead of arguing" point of view, and the fixture-drift explanation (names, tickets, numbers and files are checked by `grit-kept.md`); at most a few words change; no forced grit, no added opinions, no new closer. An output identical to the draft is the correct result and passes.

graders.evidence:

Today: pairing with Ploy on the invoice export. She thinks the CSV encoder is the slow part, I think it's the N+1 on customer lookups. We'll profile it instead of arguing.

Blocker: still waiting on staging DB creds from ops (asked Tuesday, ticket OPS-91).

cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:humanize` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:humanize"`) on `docs/rollout.md`. The reader is the engineering team; genre is prose (D), English only.

Work through the skill's loop (draft, "still AI" bullets, final) in your turn, then make your final message the final rewrite only, verbatim, with nothing before or after it.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.graderMarkdown: A forced triad is three adjectives or abstract phrases stacked in a row for rhythm, such as "robust, scalable, and seamless" or "careful, data-driven, and collaborative". A list of three concrete facts (a file, a number, a date) is not one. Score 0 only if you can copy, word for word from the final rewrite, three such adjectives or abstract phrases that sit next to each other in one sentence. Otherwise score 1.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: feature flag for the new checkout

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which puts 5% of traffic on the new checkout flow and keeps the rest on the old one. On 2026-08-30 the error rate in that 5% cohort was 3%, against 0.4% on the control. The gap traces back to the new address validator running against legacy carts.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown: Score 1 only if all hold in the final rewrite: it is UI-actual (says the payment did not go through and what the user does next: retry, check the card or balance, or contact the bank or support) with no line about the team's commitment, the user's experience, or "protecting your security"; it is at most three short sentences plus an optional one-line heading, well under half the source's length; the decline is said in Thai (ไม่สำเร็จ / ถูกปฏิเสธ / ไม่ผ่าน) rather than as the inline "(Declined)" parenthetical; particles are at most one ค่ะ/ครับ.
